messages.author: 132678befc181647
messages.subject: Problem in removing an individual
parts:
Karl: 

 

I am having a problem in removing a “bad” individual from a large soybean population of >2000 F2 individuals (actually this large pop is combined set of 8 pops that originated from the same parental mating, each with 250-260 F2s ).  

 

See the below jittermap summary for details. 

 

In trying to remove a specific individual, the below command didn’t work:

> OBJNAME <- subset(OBJNAME, ind = -1018)

Warning message:

In subset.cross(OBJNAME, ind = -1018) : Retained only one individual!

 

However, when I just arbitrarily reduced the ind number to three digits or less, the command worked as expected:

> OBJNAME1 <- subset(OBJNAME, ind = -918)

> 

 

This seems to be a bug , but maybe I just missing something here. 

If it is a bug and you can suggest a work-around, I would be very appreciative! 

 

> jittermap(OBJNAME, amount=1e-6)

messages.subject: RE: [Rqtl-disc] Problem in removing an individual
parts:
In the *.csv files, the first row is indeed a phenotype I named ID (in caps) and it has the numbers 1001, 1002, 1003,

and on up etc. for each F2 plant.  The ID numbers are not consecutive (some F2 plants were lost), and the first digit

of the 4-digit number is actually pop number that identifies the 8 combined pops in OBJNAME.

 

When I use the cmd getid(OBJNAME), I get a list of 1 to 2068 consecutive numbered individuals as shown in brief below.

 

> getid(OBJNAME)
   [1] 1001 1002 1003 1004 1005 1006 1007 1008 1009 1010 1011 1012 1013 1014
  [15] 1015 1016 1017 1018 1019 1020 1021 1022 1023 1024 1025 1027 1028 1029
. . . . .

 [911] 4140 4141 4142 4143 4144 4145 4146 4147 4148 4149 4150 4151 4152 4153
 [925] 4154 4155 4156 4157 4158 4159 4160 4161 4162 4163 4164 4165 4166 4167
 [939] 4168 4169 4170 4171 4172 4173 4174 4175 4176 4177 4178 4179 4180 4181
 [953] 4182 4183 4184 4185 4186 4187 4188 4189 4190 4191 4192 4193 4194 4195
 [967] 4196 4197 4198 4199 4200 4201 4202 4203 4204 4205 4206 4207 4208 4209
 [981] 4210 4211 4212 4213 4214 4215 4216 4217 4218 4219 4220 4221 4222 4223
 [995] 4224 4225 4226 4227 4228 4229 4230 4231 4232 4233 4234 4235 4236 4237
[1009] 4239 4240 4241 4242 4243 4244 4245 4246 4247 4248 4249 4250 4251 4252
.......

[2045] 9247 9248 9249 9250 9251 9252 9253 9254 9255 9256 9257 9258 9259 9260
[2059] 9261 9262 9263 9264 9265 9266 9267 9268 9269 9270

The red-fonted F2 ID number of 4247 is the one I wanted to drop (outlier - very few XO)

and because it was 1018th on the above list, I tried using the below subset cmd that did

not work.  This was odd, because the subset cmd did work with F2 ID numbers of three

digits or less (i.e., 999 or less), but did not work with F2 ID numbers that were 4 digits.  

For that reason, I thought that it might be a bug related to the number of digits 

accessible (no more than 3?) by the variable "ind" (1 to 2068) in the subset cmd. 

Hope that this background helps you in discerning the problem. 

 

Jim
